Hi Lena / Will,

Thanks again for the productive renewal prep call last week. Attached is a compact proposal (redwood_proposal_v3.pdf) that tries to balance Acme's need for predictable capacity with your occasional high-throughput bursts. Key concept summary below: 

- Retainer (committed monthly baseline) sized to cover 80% of observed steady-state Q3/Q4 usage.
- Burst-trigger lane: automatic soft-burst capacity unlocked when 7-day rolling usage > 120% of baseline; billed at a lower incremental rate than pure on-demand.
- Defer-conversion option: if you choose multi-year pricing, you can defer auto-renew conversion for up to 30 days post-term if usage materially drops — we provide a smoothing credit to avoid penalizing short-term variance.
- Co-terming approach: convert any add-on seat/throughput purchases to the master term on the next fiscal quarter boundary with prorated credits.

If this structure looks sensible, can you confirm 1) preferred invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly) and 2) procurement's timeline for redlines? I'll loop legal and Marissa in once you confirm.

Also attaching a usage projection (usage_projection_q4.xlsx) we modeled from your last six months. Happy to walk through numbers.

Best,
Jordan

Jordan / Connor — ran the numbers and drafted a concise term-sheet. Summary: 

- Quarterly invoicing impact: 1.8% price uplift on committed retainer when switching from monthly to quarterly (finance prefers to keep monthly but will accept quarterly with uplift).
- Burst lane pricing: set incremental rate at 0.65x of current on-demand for the 7-day trigger window; cap soft-burst at 2x baseline in any 30-day rolling window to limit exposure.
- Defer-conversion clause (suggested language): "Customer may elect a single 30-day deferment of auto-renew upon written notice no later than 15 days prior to renewal; during the deferment period Redwood will apply a smoothing credit equal to 50% of the difference between committed and realized usage for up to one billing cycle."

Action items I recommend we take to Acme: 
1) Offer quarterly invoicing option with a small uplift (1.8%) and call it out in sheet.
2) Include the defer-conversion clause verbatim and add an example calculation to avoid ambiguity.
3) Ask Acme to sign a short amendment that co-terms add-ons at the next fiscal quarter boundary (prorated) — keeps their ops simpler.

I've attached a one-page priced term-sheet and an example smoothing credit calc. Happy to stand up a 20-min call with procurement if you want to walk them through.

Marissa
